question: Where do antibodies come from in passive immunity?

options.A: Bone marrow stem cells create them following a vaccination
options.B: T-lymphocytes manufacture them upon direct pathogen exposure
options.C: The recipient's own plasma cells produce them after infection
options.D: Antibodies are transferred ready-made from another source

explanation: Passive immunity relies entirely on receiving pre-made antibodies rather than manufacturing them internally. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h1)

question: Why doesn't passive immunity give long-term protection?

options.A: The recipient's immune cells fail to develop memory cells
options.B: Pathogens mutate too quickly for transferred antibodies to bind
options.C: White blood cells actively destroy all foreign immunoglobulins
options.D: The liver metabolizes the antibodies into inactive amino acids

explanation: Because the body is never exposed to the antigen to trigger its own response, no memory cells are created. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h1)

question: Which antibody crosses the human placenta to protect the foetus?
explanation: IgG is the only antibody type that can cross the placental barrier to provide passive immunity to the unborn baby. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h2)

question: Why is a baby born prematurely at 28 weeks at a higher risk of infection?

options.A: Breast milk completely lacks antibodies during the first month of life
options.B: Premature infants produce their own active white blood cells too quickly
options.C: They missed the critical period of transplacental IgG transfer in late pregnancy
options.D: Their mucosal membranes cannot secrete any form of protective IgA

explanation: Most maternal IgG transfer happens during the third trimester, so early preterm babies are born with very low antibody stores. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h2)

question: When is artificial passive immunity usually given to a patient?

options.A: Years before planned travel to build lifelong immune memory
options.B: When immediate protection is needed after a high-risk exposure
options.C: Once a chronic infection has fully established itself in tissues
options.D: As a routine replacement for standard childhood vaccines

explanation: Artificial passive immunity provides instant antibodies for urgent situations where waiting for active immunization is unsafe. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h3)

question: What is the main difference between artificial passive immunity and active vaccination?

options.A: Passive immunity supplies ready-made antibodies instead of stimulating the body to make them
options.B: Vaccines protect only temporarily whereas passive therapy lasts a lifetime
options.C: Vaccines provide instantaneous protection while passive products take weeks to work
options.D: Passive immunity relies on live weakened viruses rather than killed bacteria

explanation: Active vaccines force the immune system to build its own defense, while passive immunity hands over external antibodies. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h3)

question: How quickly does passive immunity begin protecting the body after administration?
explanation: Because the antibodies are already fully formed, they start neutralizing target agents right away without any delay. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h4)

question: What happens to passive antibodies in the human body over time?

options.A: They are gradually broken down and cleared from circulation
options.B: They bind permanently to host tissues and remain there forever
options.C: They transform into active memory cells to fight future infections
options.D: They multiply inside the bone marrow to form a permanent reserve

explanation: The body treats introduced antibodies like any other circulating protein, breaking them down over several weeks or months. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h4)

question: A woman with a rhesus-negative blood type gives birth to a rhesus-positive baby in a clinic. What is the best action?

options.A: Give the newborn a live polio vaccine immediately to stimulate active immunity
options.B: Schedule the mother for routine tetanus toxoid booster injections next week
options.C: Provide oral broad-spectrum antibiotics to clear maternal white blood cells
options.D: Administer anti-D immunoglobulin to prevent maternal antibody sensitization

explanation: Anti-D immunoglobulin clears any fetal cells that entered the mother's blood, stopping her immune system from forming antibodies against future rhesus-positive babies. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard use of passive immunisation?

options.A: Stopping rhesus incompatibility reactions in pregnant women
options.B: Preventing disease after a deep puncture wound contaminated with soil
options.C: Providing immediate antibody cover following a rabid animal bite
options.D: Building lifelong immunity through routine childhood measles vaccination

explanation: Vaccines stimulate active immunity and long-term memory, which is different from passive immunization. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h5)

question: Why can someone who received passive antibodies for tetanus still catch tetanus months later?

options.A: The body formed no memory cells to recognize the bacteria in the future
options.B: The original antibodies mutated into harmful antigens over time
options.C: Live bacteria destroyed all the circulating white blood cells
options.D: The initial dose permanently suppressed the patient's bone marrow

explanation: Passive immunity bypasses the body's immune learning process, leaving no memory cells to protect against later infections. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h6)

question: What is a known complication of using animal-derived antisera?

options.A: Excessive production of endogenous red blood cells
options.B: Permanent transformation of recipient blood type
options.D: Immediate lifelong immunity to multiple viruses

explanation: Foreign proteins from animal sera can cause allergic or adverse immune reactions in humans, such as serum sickness. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T8#BMP111_U6_T8_h6)
